오늘 챙겨야 할 해외 이슈

1) 장기미국채 금리 급등과 글로벌 채권 매도세 심화 왜 지금 지켜봐야 하나: 미국 10년물 수익률이 약 5.15%, 30년물이 5.45%를 넘나들며 수십 년래 고점권에 있고, 독일·일본 등도 동반 상승해 전세계 금융여건이 빠르게 타이트해지고 있다. 유가 100달러대, 인플레이션 지속, 재정적자/국채공급 확대 기대가 장기금리를 밀어올렸고, 프랑스-독일 국채 스프레드는 2012년대 수준으로 벌어졌다. 모기지 등 실물 차입비용 상승, 주식·크레딧 리스크 프리미엄 확대, 미 재무부의 경매·바이백 운용과 그 시장 반응까지 자산군 전반에 파급될 수 있어 추세 투자자는 금리·듀레이션 민감 자산의 상관구조 변화를 점검할 필요가 있다. 2) 달러 강세 재개와 엔화 개입 리스크, 유럽통화 약세 왜 지금 지켜봐야 하나: 미 금리 급등과 연준 추가 긴축 베팅이 강화되며 달러가 2주 연속 강세를 보이는 반면, 유로는 2개월래 저점권, 파운드는 3개월래 저점권이다. 엔화는 3주 저점 부근에서 당국 개입 가능성이 재부각되고 BOJ 추가 조치 기대/경계가 교차한다. 에너지 가격 상승과 지정학 변수(중동, 글로벌 성장 데이터)가 환율과 위험선호를 흔드는 구도가며, 이는 원자재 가격, 신흥시장·수출주, 글로벌 매크로 헤지 포지션의 변동성을 키울 수 있다. 3) 유가 100달러대 회귀와 디젤·수송비 상승, 중동 리스크 왜 지금 지켜봐야 하나: 공급 차질 우려로 유가가 105달러 선까지 뛰었다가 중동 평화 시사 보도로 되돌림이 있었지만, 디젤·에너지 비용 상승과 미국의 디젤 수출 제한 논의 등은 비용 인플레이션 압력을 자극했다. S&P 글로벌 조사에서는 연료·운송 투입비 상승이 확인됐고, 이는 물가 지표와 연준 경로 기대, 장기금리 레벨에 재차 영향을 줄 수 있다. 에너지 민감 업종·국가, 운송비·마진에 노출된 기업군, 인플레이션 헤지 수단의 상관관계가 흔들릴 수 있어 모니터링이 필요하다. 4) 연준 커뮤니케이션과 ‘금리 vs. 성장’ 딜레마 심화 왜 지금 지켜봐야 하나: 시장은 10월 추가 인상 확률을 높게 반영하고 있고(일부 추정치 약 70%), 연준 인사(예: 윌리엄스)의 매파적 발언이 이어지는 가운데, 급등한 장기금리가 사실상 긴축 효과를 내는 상황이어서 정책 대응의 미묘한 균형이 요구된다. CNBC 보도는 채권금리 급등이 연준의 신뢰와 경기 둔화 리스크 사이에서 정책판단을 어렵게 만든다고 지적했고, 재정조달·원자재 요인 등 금리 상승의 성격을 해석하는 데 의견이 엇갈린다. 이는 포워드 가이던스 의존도 축소 국면에서 금리·달러·위험자산의 변동성에 직접 연결될 수 있다. 5) 단기 촉매: 미국 고용·물가 지표(다음 주)와 미·중 정상회담 등 지정학 이벤트 왜 지금 지켜봐야 하나: 다음 주 미국 고용보고서(10/2)와 물가 지표(PCE 등)는 연준의 연내 경로에 대한 시장가격을 재조정할 수 있는 고빈도 촉매다. 동시에 트럼프-시진핑 회담, 미-이란 긴장 고조 가능성 등이 거시 리스크 프리미엄과 원자재·환율 변동을 자극하고 있다. 최근 10년물 급등 국면이 주식 변동성 확대와 맞물려 왔던 이력상, 데이터·외교 이벤트가 현재의 금리/달러 추세와 어떤 조합을 만드는지 주시할 필요가 있다. 참고: 위 이슈들은 ‘무엇을 지켜볼지’에 대한 정리일 뿐이며, 특정 자산의 향후 방향을 단정하거나 보유 판단을 변경하지 않는다.

Surging Treasury yields pose a brand new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
Jeff Cox · 2026-09-24T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The CNBC piece argues that surging Treasury yields have created a delicate dilemma for the Federal Reserve under Chairman Kevin Warsh. A sharper-than-expected rise in yields reflects bets on higher policy rates in response to persistent inflation, energy price pressures, and global financing dynamics. Markets increasingly price in multiple rate hikes (including Oct and possibly later in 2027), while some Wall Street strategists warn against overreacting and warn that yields may be reacting to oil-price volatility and implied stronger growth rather than just inflation. Key tensions: - The Fed risks either stifling the economy with too-aggressive tightening or losing credibility if it eases off in the face of sticky inflation. - Warsh’s approach of letting market signals guide policy contrasts with prior forward guidance, complicating the decision process when yields surge. - Market signals suggest a hawkish tilt, but some strategists caution that the rise in yields may overstate the need for aggressive tightening. Bottom line: Global macro dynamics, energy prices, and debt issuance are driving higher Treasury yields, pressuring the Fed to balance credibility and economic activity. Warsh faces a policy crossroads: respond to market-implied tightening or risk misreading inflation signals and market expectations, with considerable volatility possible if guidance remains ambiguous.

오늘은 위험자산이 전반적으로 중립(HOLD)인 반면, 안전자산 중 채권과 금이 동시에 매도로 눌려 있는 조합이 이어지며, 시장이 뚜렷한 위험 선호로 치고 나가진 않지만 안전판에 대한 수요도 약화된 상태임을 시사한다. 최근 흐름을 보면 9/22에 기술주와 천연가스가 잠깐 매수로 점등됐지만 곧바로 중립으로 되돌아와, 단기 ‘리스크 온’ 신호가 확산되기보다 소강 국면으로 흡수된 모습이다. 채권은 특히 중장기물에서 매도가 꾸준히 유지되고 금도 동일 방향이라, 전통적 헤지 축이 함께 약한 동조화를 보이고 있고, 이는 달러가 뚜렷한 추세 없이 중립이라는 점과 결합해 특정 통화 요인보다는 금리·실질수익률 측면의 압력이 상대적으로 두드러졌음을 암시한다. 원자재는 대체로 중립 속에 농산물이 유독 매도로 이탈해 섹터 내 괴리가 두드러지는데, 에너지와 광산·산업금속이 방향을 정하지 못하는 가운데 식료·농가공 가격만 약세 신호가 분명하다는 점이 눈에 띈다. 종합하면, 위험·안전축이 같은 방향으로 질주하지 않는 ‘대기 모드’ 속에서, 헤지 자산 약세가 반복 확인되고 단기적 동조화 시도는 금세 되돌려진, 관망 기조의 하루다.

Fed Hikes: What's Next for Treasury Yields?
www.advisorperspectives.com · 2026-09-23T18:30:39.000Z

Summary of US long-term treasury bond yields outlook (per Advisor Perspectives commentary) - Our view: Long-term yields may stay in a higher range. The 10-year yield is near 5% and likely to hover roughly in the 4.5%–5% area for now, rather than return quickly to prior lower levels. - Why yields stay elevated: Persistent inflation, a resilient economy, and fiscal considerations keep upside risks to yields ahead of downside risks. The typical historical relationship between the 10-year yield and the fed funds peak has shifted in recent cycles. - Strategy for investors: Favor a below-benchmark average duration (short- to intermediate-term bonds) rather than adding long-duration exposure. The ascent in yields offers income opportunities and potential price cushions via higher coupons. - Timing for longer bonds: Tactically, adding longer-duration exposure isn’t favored yet, but could become more attractive if upside risk to long-term yields materializes and/or the economic outlook weakens, suggesting a shift toward longer maturities. - What could change the view: If inflation remains high and the Fed raises rates beyond expectations, short- and intermediate-term bonds could underperform; if the economy slows meaningfully, longer-duration bonds may become more attractive. - Practical take: Two- to three-year Treasuries currently offer higher yields than many shorter bills, providing income with a modest duration. Investors should weigh their horizons and risk tolerance; the focus remains on higher yields rather than waiting for further rate hikes to stop.

Key takeaways relevant to a US Treasury yields outlook: - Long-end yields have risen about 100 bps over the last six months, with the U.S. 10-year participating in the climb. - While deficits have been a driver, other forces have dominated recently; this shift could matter for term premiums if deficits worsen. - Deteriorating fiscal deficits and higher interest burdens could expand term premiums, pushing longer maturities higher. - Fiscal sustainability, combined with rate hikes and political attention, may increasingly influence the Treasury curve and long-end yield expectations. Implication for US Treasury bond yields outlook: If deficits continue to widen and rate burdens persist, expect support for higher long-end yields and steeper term premium adjustments, potentially elevating the forward path for 10-year and longer maturities.

Global bond selloff deepens, U.S. 30-year yields highest since '04
www.bnnbloomberg.ca · 2026-09-24T00:00:00.000Z

US Treasury bond yields outlook (based on the article) - The global bond selloff intensified, pushing U.S. long-dated yields higher. The 30-year yield rose above 5.46%, its highest since 2004, while the 10-year hit about 5.14%. - Drivers: persistent inflation pressures from high energy costs, resilient economic growth, and substantial government spending. The selloff has been amplified by strong U.S. activity data and expectations of continued Fed rate hikes. - Market implications: - Bond prices declining as yields rise; longer maturities are more sensitive to financing of government deficits. - Mortgage costs rising (30-year mortgage around 7%), contributing to consumer pressure. - Shorter-term yields follow rate-hike expectations; the 30-year yield reflects longer-horizon funding risks. - Investor sentiment: despite near-term resilience (growth, profits, AI-driven spending), a high-funding-cost environment and fiscal deficits may increase volatility and potential market turbulence. - Outlook considerations: - Sustained above-trend growth and ongoing deficits could keep long yields elevated. - The pace of inflation and any shifts in Fed policy will be key drivers for the trajectory of the 30-year and other long-end yields.

DBA농산물 (Agriculture)매도종가 28.54
추천: 매도 근거 - 기계적 신호: 종가 28.54가 트레일링 스탑 28.67 아래로 하락해 청산 신호가 발생했습니다. 동시에 20일/100일 Donchian 상단 돌파 여부가 모두 False이므로 신규 매수 조건도 충족하지 않습니다. 규칙상 보유가 아닌 매도(청산)가 정답입니다. - 뉴스 해석(추세 확인용 팩트 체크): - Agri-Access의 9월 WASDE 요약: 옥수수·대두의 기말재고가 타이트해지며 2026-27 시즌 평균가격 전망이 상향(옥수수 $4.80, 대두 $12). 이는 중기적으로 농산물 가격을 지지하는 팩트지만, 현재 DBA 가격은 상단 돌파로 추세 재개를 확인하지 못했고 오히려 스탑을 이탈했습니다. 즉, 펀더멘털은 우호적일 수 있으나 가격이 추세로 입증하지 못했으므로 지금의 청산 신호를 뒤집을 근거는 아닙니다. - Agweek의 날씨 시장 분석: 미국 수확·품질 변수와 브라질 파종·강우가 근시일 내 방향성을 좌우할 것이라는 내용으로, 단기 변동성은 설명하지만 즉각적인 상단 돌파 추세를 보장하진 않습니다. 스탑 이탈 후 보유를 정당화할 신뢰도 높은 추세 팩트로 보기 어렵습니다. - 보조 참고(일목): 구름 위·양운으로 상방 편향이 보이지만 이는 보조지표일 뿐, 매도/보유 결정을 바꾸지 않습니다. 다만 재돌파(20일/100일 Donchian 상단 종가 상향 돌파) 발생 시에는 재진입을 고려하되, 구름 신호와의 괴리를 감안해 초기 비중을 다소 보수적으로 시작했다가 추세 확정 시 증액하는 접근이 합리적입니다. 액션 - 현재 포지션: 전량 청산. - 재진입 트리거: 종가의 Donchian 채널 상단 상향 돌파 발생 시에만 매수 재개. 신규 매수 후에는 최근 고점 - 3×ATR로 트레일링 스탑을 즉시 갱신해 관리.

Crop Prices Rise Again in the September WASDE | Agri-Access
www.agri-access.com · 2026-09-21T00:00:00.000Z

Summary of "Crop Prices Rise Again in the September WASDE | Agri-Access" (relevant to agricultural commodities market outlook analysis) - The USDA’s September WASDE shifts focus from yield/acres to overall supply-demand balance, tightening ending stocks for corn and soybeans and supporting price forecasts. - Corn: national yield forecast reduced by 2.2 bu/ac to 178.5, harvested acres down, production down to 15.8 billion bu. Lower supply with unchanged exports lifts the 2026-27 season-average price to $4.80/bu (+$0.30). - Soybeans: yield up slightly by 0.1 bu/ac to 52.8, higher harvested acres, production modestly higher, but exports up 25 million bu. Stronger demand reduces ending stocks to 310 million bu and raises the season-average price to $12.00/bu (+$0.60). - Key takeaway: price support driven by tighter ending stocks—corn from reduced supply, soybeans from stronger demand. - Broader grain view: wheat supply/use unchanged; 2026-27 farm price forecast raised to $6.40/bu. Cotton: lower production/yield/ending stocks but higher projected price (upland cotton at 78 cents/lb). - Implications for lenders: improved revenue outlook for crop borrowers but not a substitute for breakeven analysis. Profitability still hinges on yield, costs, crop mix, insurance, inputs, storage, interest, and marketing decisions. - Practical implications: a more favorable price environment exists, yet margin outcomes vary by operation. Corn priced at about $4.80/bu and soybeans at $12.00/bu are supportive but require operation-specific risk assessment, including basis, regional yields, and marketing windows. - Additional context: producers’ margins and credit risk will depend on local factors (basis, harvest timing, demand, global trade) and the ability to manage costs and protect margins through hedging and marketing strategies.

Commodity Market Outlook: Trends Driving Optimism in 2026
Morgan Stanley · 2026-01-25T16:35:04.749Z

Summary: - The Morgan Stanley outlook for agricultural commodities in 2026 is cautiously optimistic. After 2020s volatility, supply chains are stabilizing, with strong harvests and adequate inventories helping softer, more affordable prices in many regions. - Price stability reduces downside risk from spikes, though selective opportunities exist (e.g., coffee pricing experienced weather-driven spikes in 2025). - Global demand for agricultural goods is expected to rise due to growing populations and higher incomes, particularly in emerging markets. This supports expanding agricultural trade and profits for agro-exporters. - Innovation and new uses (biofuels, plant-based products) could create additional growth channels for certain crops. - Overall, the sector benefits from broader structural trends (e.g., energy transition) that may boost demand for related agricultural inputs and technology-enabled logistics, while price volatility remains a risk from geopolitics or weather shocks. - Takeaway for investors: opportunities may arise from price stabilization in staples, selective beta in crops with supply risks (like coffee), and growth via tech-enabled efficiency and new markets, but remain mindful of macro and climate risks.

Summer is over, but the weather market isn't - Agweek | #1 source for agriculture news, farming, markets
www.agweek.com · 2026-09-25T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The U.S. and global weather outlook is shaping a fall agricultural commodities market unlike past years. In the U.S., the focus shifts from boosting yields to preserving harvested bushels amid potential rain, wind, or lodging that could reduce binning and quality. USDA projections place corn at 178.5 bu/ac and soybeans at 52.8 bu/ac, though actual harvest data is still needed to confirm. In Brazil, planting for 2026-27 soybeans has begun, with irregular rainfall and reliance on irrigated areas; the timing and volume of rains will influence both soybeans and the subsequent safrinha corn crop. El Niño may bring a wetter southern U.S. pattern and drier northern conditions, affecting harvest windows and regional crop quality. Trade and demand, particularly involving China, will continue to drive markets, but supply dynamics—U.S. harvest progress and Brazil’s planting rains—will largely determine near-term direction.

JPMorgan Warns El Niño Will Tighten Grip on Global Agriculture from Early 2027
www.zyotwdhon.com · 2026-09-20T00:00:00.000Z

JPMorgan warns that the full impact of the current El Niño on global agriculture is still ahead, with the most pronounced effects expected to emerge from Q1 2027. Key points: - El Niño likely to intensify through late 2026 and peak around November, with very strong conditions likely in the Northern Hemisphere autumn/winter. - Structural pressures—high diesel prices, fertilizer shortages, and ongoing geopolitical trade disruptions—amplify risk to crop production worldwide. - Regions at higher risk: Southeast Asia (palm oil, rice); India (rice, cotton, oilseeds); Brazil and Argentina (soybeans, corn, coffee, sugar, cocoa). - Near-term price dynamics: JPMorgan’s agricultural index reached multiyear highs in August; prior breakout levels may provide support on pullbacks, indicating sustained upside momentum in agricultural commodities. - Carryover inventories from past harvests may cushion near-term shocks but are not expected to offset the deeper 2027 impact. Bottom line for agricultural commodities market outlook: elevated risk and potential price upside persist into 2027 as El Niño drives tighter supply, reinforced by existing energy, fertilizer, and geopolitics headwinds.

Kharif Sowing Nears Normal, But Overall Acreage Remains Lower by Amit Gupta, Kedia Advisory
investmentguruindia.com · 2026-09-21T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - India’s 2026 Kharif sowing as of 18 Sep stands at 1,103.90 lakh ha, down 15.05 lakh ha (1.35%) from last year. - Rice area: 429.28 lakh ha, down 3.73% YoY. - Pulses: up 1.45% to 119.65 lakh ha, led by higher sowing of tur and urad. - Oilseeds: largely flat at 194.76 lakh ha; sesamum and sunflower up (sunflower +84.34%, sesamum +13.22%), soybean down 0.72%, groundnut slightly down, castorseed down 9.05%. - Coarse cereals: marginal increase; jowar +9.39%, bajra +3.29%, maize -2.23%. - Cotton: area down 0.90% to 109.61 lakh ha. - Outlook: Overall Kharif acreage remains below last year, supporting prices for weaker-sown crops. Mixed crop signals: pulses and some oilseeds strengthen supply expectations, while rice, soybean, groundnut, and cotton show declines that could keep market concerns over supply in focus. Prices are likely to be selectively supported with a mixed, crop-specific outlook. Context for traders/investors: - Lower rice and key oilseed areas may support prices in those segments. - Strong pulses and some coarse cereals could cap downside pressures. - Watch ongoing weather trends and regional sowing shifts for near-term price direction.
